clauses.reason: The order exempts Louis A. Simon, Supervising Architect of the Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of six months ending November 30, 1941". The recital says Louis A. Simon had been exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling four years by Executive Orders No. 7581 of March 19, 1937, No. 7824 of February 25, 1938, No. 8046 of February 11, 1939, and No. 8369 of March 7, 1940; those earlier orders precede this one and are not events of it. The end is recorded as November 30, 1941 (1941-11-30), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative.

research_rationale:
EO 8747 is a one-person retirement exemption. Identity: the held text is the American Presidency Project page (node 371709, Common Crawl capture 2025-11-07T21:09:04Z); the page record with the same sha256 has a heading naming Executive Order 8747, the date 1941-04-28 that matches the signature date in the text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file. The text was read in full: one recital paragraph, one operative sentence, signature and date. Inventory: a single clause, the exemption of Louis A. Simon. End: the stated period gives 1941-11-30 as the first end by the order's own terms.  The packet's machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, OFR catalog, and held-text person-name search) record no hit that revokes, supersedes or shortens the order. The OFR-catalog search returned 4 hit(s) for this order; the held edge records show them to be cross-reference or amendment notes linking this order to the same employee's earlier exemption orders, and none names a later order that affects it. The record rests on a transcription: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

savings.reason: The order contains no sentence that operates after November 30, 1941 and no savings clause. Service that Louis A. Simon rendered while the exemption was in force is a completed fact that the end of the period does not undo; that is the only effect that outlasts the order.
